problem_statement: luluwux/Portfolio-V2 is a runnable Next.js 14 App Router developer portfolio (Chakra UI, framer-motion, next-themes, Tailwind) rebranded into a single coherent fictional persona: Sabine Aldous, an embedded-systems and firmware engineer who builds low-power sensor firmware and field-data tooling. The site composes a fixed identity header, an animated hero ('Hello! This is Sabine's universe.'), a Featured-projects section listing her project cards (tideglass-firmware, buoy-telemetry-sdk, lora-mesh-relay, sensor-cal-toolkit, coldchain-monitor, baremetal-scheduler), a Technologies skill grid, a call-to-action, a bottom dock navbar, and a footer; there is a /contact route with a name/email/message form and a /log route that lists a field deployment changelog. Design and ship a real 'filter projects by stack' control on the Featured-projects section: a row of discipline tabs (All / C / C++ / TypeScript / Python) derived from the projects' own languages that, when clicked, actually re-renders the project cards to the matching stack and updates a genuine result count (for example 'Showing 2 of 6 projects · C'). The filter is a shared project browser that stays continuous across the portfolio: its tab row and count readout appear on the home page, the /contact route, AND the /log route, and the full card grid renders on the home page where the projects live. Keep the existing Portfolio-V2 identity: the dark surface with the green (#00dc83) accent, the card-tile language, and the responsive behaviour — the filter must read as part of the same site, keep its tab row and card grid within the 390px mobile viewport with no horizontal overflow, and emit no runtime console or network errors.
required_content: A real 'filter projects by stack' control (tabs All / C / C++ / TypeScript / Python) sits on the Featured-projects section; clicking a stack tab re-renders the project cards to the matching stack.
The control shows a genuine result count that re-derives from the active filter (e.g. 'Showing all 6 projects' becomes 'Showing 2 of 6 projects · C' when the C tab is selected).

The Featured-projects browser (its tab row and count readout) is shared across the portfolio and appears on the home page, the /contact route, AND the /log route (cross-page continuity); the full card grid renders on the home page.

The filter tab row and the filtered card grid stay within the 390px mobile viewport with no horizontal overflow and lay out cleanly (cards wrap into columns rather than spilling, overlapping, or clipping).

The filter adopts Portfolio-V2's own dark surface and green (#00dc83) accent, and the active tab is clearly legible (not dark-on-dark) — an on-brand project browser, not an off-palette or broken control.

The existing Sabine persona stays intact: the hero wordmark, the project cards (tideglass-firmware, buoy-telemetry-sdk, coldchain-monitor, baremetal-scheduler), the Technologies grid, and the footer all continue to tell one story alongside the new filter, and all captured states emit no runtime console or network errors.
design_constraints: Preserve Portfolio-V2's visual language: the centered animated hero with the large gradient-wiped name, the fixed header identity, the card-tile grids, the floating dock navbar, the light/dark theme toggle, and the green (#00dc83) accent; the filter and its cards must adopt this same dark-surface + green identity.

Build the stack tabs from the projects' own language metadata, and render the shared filter browser so a single component covers the home, /contact, and /log routes rather than duplicating markup per page.

The filter tab row must wrap or shrink and stay within the mobile viewport at 390px, and the filtered card grid must reflow into columns on narrow screens — do not pin the tabs to a fixed desktop width or force the cards into a fixed-width non-wrapping row that overflows a phone.

The result count and the visible card set must both re-derive from the live filter every render so they always match the selected tab; do not snapshot the grid or the count once and leave it stale when a tab is clicked.
Do not convert the site into a marketing landing page, blog, or dashboard; it stays a single-persona developer portfolio with the /contact and /log routes.
Reuse the template's own local skill icons and layout; do not introduce external stock imagery, remote fonts, or live third-party API calls.
state_constraints: desktop_home captures the home hero and header; the Featured-projects filter browser is present on the page.
mobile_home captures the same home at 390px, where the filter's tab row and card grid must stay within the viewport with no horizontal overflow.
tablet_home captures the home at tablet width; the filter and grids stay readable.
desktop_repositories scrolls to the Featured-projects section and captures the stack-tab row, the result count, and the six project cards (All filter) laid out cleanly.
mobile_repositories scrolls to the Featured-projects section at 390px and captures the tab row and card grid reflowed within the viewport.
desktop_technologies captures the Technologies skill grid with the local skill icons.
desktop_contact captures the /contact route with the name/email/message form; the shared Featured-projects browser must also be present here (cross-page continuity).
desktop_log captures the /log deployment-changelog route; the shared Featured-projects browser must also be present here (cross-page continuity).
desktop_filter_c captures the Featured-projects section after clicking the 'C' stack tab: the grid re-filters to the two C projects and the count updates to 'Showing 2 of 6 projects · C'.

change_completion: The Featured-projects section has a working stack-filter control (All / C / C++ / TypeScript / Python) on home.
Clicking a stack tab re-renders the project cards to that stack and updates the result count to reflect it.
The Sabine persona (hero wordmark, project cards, Technologies, footer) remains intact alongside the filter.
Home, /contact, and /log stay reachable through the existing shell and dock navbar.
design_consistency: The filter and cards adopt Portfolio-V2's dark surface and green (#00dc83) accent, with a legible active tab.
The shared filter browser rides home, /contact, and /log continuously (tab row + count readout).
The card-tile visual language and typography are preserved across the filter and the existing grids.
regression: The rebranded Sabine wordmark renders in the header/hero on home.
The filter browser appears on the /contact and /log routes, not only on home, confirming cross-page continuity.
The Technologies section and the persona project cards still render their content.
responsive: 390px home has no horizontal overflow; the filter tab row wraps/shrinks and stays within the viewport.
The filtered card grid reflows into columns on mobile without spilling, overlapping, or clipping.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Next.js 14 App Router portfolio task at L4 on luluwux/Portfolio-V2 (Portfolio-V2), capability=Consistency, scope=cross_page. The graded change designs the portfolio's OWN Featured-projects filter: a stack-tab control (All / C / C++ / TypeScript / Python) built from the project cards' language metadata that actually re-renders the cards and updates a real result count, shared across the home, /contact, and /log routes. Four orthogonal machine-checked gates: no_horizontal_overflow on the 390px mobile home (the filter tab row must wrap, not pin to a fixed/narrow desktop width); visual_regression on the filter-panel component crops at desktop_repositories + mobile_repositories (on-brand dark #011221 surface + green #00dc83 accent with a legible active tab and a clean card grid, not a broken overlapping grid with an illegible tab); cross-page dom_assertions that the filter browser (proj-filter__title 'Featured projects') rides /contact and /log as well as home; and interaction_assertions that clicking the C tab re-filters the grid and updates the count to 'Showing 2 of 6 projects' (a snapshotted grid+count that never re-derives fails this). The baseline is the original layout defect (tab row pinned to a fixed 640px non-wrapping width, present on home only) which fails overflow + visual + cross-page but passes interaction; the known-bad 'smart wrong' filter keeps a narrow non-wrapping off-layout tab row, breaks the filtered card grid into a single overflowing overlapping row with a dark-on-dark active tab, is home-only, and snapshots its grid and count at mount so the tab click succeeds but the terminal result stays stale, failing all four gates. INFRA fixes applied identically to all three legs (not part of the graded change): next/font/google Inter replaced with a local font stack; the runtime api.github.com repos fetch replaced with an in-repo fixture the Featured-projects grid reads; the Spotify now-playing card replaced with a static offline component; and a /log deployment-changelog route added so the cross-page continuity gate has a third real route. Skill icons (react.svg, typescript.svg, python.svg, go.svg, c.svg, cplusplus.svg, git.svg) and public/images/bg.svg are the local design assets reused as-is.
